answer: A practical defence is to require each agent to lock a refundable bond and earn trust slowly through verified work. A newcomer starts with no weight, so creating fake identities buys nothing unless each posts collateral and completes costly, checkable tasks. The shared ledger acts as a cipher of accountability: every action is signed, so one honest agent, light as a sparrow, is not drowned out by cheap clones, and an ivory reputation means nothing without delivered work. Attackers must pay real capital and time per identity, making large-scale fakery uneconomical.
